stale_rules.HASH_MISMATCH: a stored step id differs from the id recomputed from the stored step
stale_rules.SOURCE_CHANGED: an input source id is missing from registry/sources.json, or its text no longer hashes to its id
stale_rules.ASSUMPTION_CHANGED: an assumption id on the step is missing from registry/assumptions.json, is superseded by a later entry, or its statement no longer hashes to its id
stale_rules.FIELD_CHANGED: the head step of a field differs from the step computed now from the entity file
stale_rules.INPUT_CHANGED: a parent step named in inputs is flagged by any rule above or has been superseded; applied transitively

revision_rule: Nothing is deleted or edited. A revision appends a new step whose supersedes is the prior step id. A superseded step stays in the file. An appended step whose id already exists in the file is refused.

mapping.LEXICAL_VOID: the field is null and the record states the gap in words (a note such as 'unmeasured', or a notes entry for the field)
mapping.VOID: the field is null and no reason is recorded
mapping.UNMAPPED: the field has a value and no source at all
mapping.REJECTED: a value was offered and refused by a gate; none is produced by the backfill

void_states.shape: void is null, or {state, reason}; a step with a void state for a null field has value null

snapshot_classes.use: a field on any summarized or coarse record; null on a record that is not a summary
snapshot_classes.provenance/INDEX.json: SUMMARY_ONLY (per-entity counts; the steps cannot be rebuilt from it)

thresholds: none: the chain has no numeric gate

amendments.name: existence states (source pass, stage 1)
amendments.after: the source pass plan at 4221e16; before scripts/existence_check.py existed and before any search was sent. The entity ranking below was already visible when this was written; its rule is the one used throughout (count descending, id ascending).
amendments.what: What an existence check is, its four states, how a match is decided, and what is written to registry/sources.json. Stage 1 checks whether a cited work can be found as cited. It reads no abstract and no full text, and it sets no status on any field.

existence_states.FOUND_AS_CITED: a PubMed record is identified and every compared item agrees with the string
existence_states.FOUND_DIFFERS: a PubMed record is identified and at least one compared item differs; each difference is listed as {item, cited, record}
existence_states.NOT_FOUND_INDEXED: PubMed was searched and no record was identified
existence_states.NOT_INDEXED: a book, book chapter or non-biomedical venue, or a string naming no work with an author and a year: not searchable here
existence_states.never: no state means 'does not exist'. A miss is a statement about one index and one search.

scope.entities: rank entities by number of attribute fields (head steps under attributes.*), descending, ties by entity id ascending; take the first 10
scope.sources: every source string that is an input of an attribute head step of those entities; near-duplicate strings are each checked separately
scope.index: PubMed through NCBI esearch and esummary (bibliographic summary records only). No efetch, no abstract, no full text.

amendments.works: a string may name several works. A work is each 'Surname (YYYY)' occurrence (with 'et al.', '& Name' or a lowercase particle allowed); its text runs to the next occurrence. Title = the first quoted text in it; venue, volume and pages are read from what follows the title.
search: 1: first-author surname [au] AND year [pdat] AND title words [ti]
2, if 1 is empty: surname [au] AND title words [ti]
a work with no quoted title: surname [au] AND year [pdat] AND up to 4 words of its description [tiab]
amendments.title_words: lowercase alphanumeric tokens of 4 or more letters, stop words removed, at most 8
amendments.identified: with a title: among at most 5 returned records, the best one whose title holds at least 0.8 of the cited title's tokens (3+ letters) and whose own tokens are at least 0.5 covered by the cited title. Without a title: only when the description query returns exactly one record.
amendments.compared_items: author (first-author surname), year (publication date year), title (token sets equal), venue (cited journal tokens contained in the record's journal name or the reverse, or an acronym of it), volume, pages (first page; last page when both give one). An item the string does not give is listed under not_compared, never counted as agreeing or differing. A work with no title, when identified, is FOUND_DIFFERS with the item 'title' cited as null.
amendments.miss_label: every work is searched first. A miss is NOT_INDEXED when the work's text carries a book or non-biomedical marker (publisher words, 'ed.', a chapter 'in', or a venue on the list in the script), else NOT_FOUND_INDEXED.
amendments.string_state: the weakest state among the string's works, in the order NOT_FOUND_INDEXED, NOT_INDEXED, FOUND_DIFFERS, FOUND_AS_CITED. A string is FOUND_AS_CITED only when every work in it is. Per-work results are kept.
amendments.registry: registry/sources.json gains 'existence' on every entry: null when not checked, else {state, matched_record, checked, works}. matched_record lists the identified records (pmid, doi, title, first_author, year, journal, volume, pages). No source string is edited and no id changes; a difference is recorded under the work's 'differs', never in place. same_as, opened and fetched are not touched.
amendments.as_received: search responses are not committed; their sha256 are listed in provenance/as_received/existence_MANIFEST.json

amendments.name: existence states: identification amended after the first run
amendments.after: the first run of scripts/existence_check.py under 81ae5f2 (166 requests). Its results were seen before this entry was written; this is a post-run change and is recorded as one.
amendments.why: The title-only search (step 3) returned records by other authors that the original rule counted as the cited work: 'Brown et al. (2020) Language models are few-shot learners' was matched to Zhang C (2026) 'Making Large Vision-Language Models Better Few-Shot Learners', and 'Hanlon & Messenger (2018) Cephalopod Behaviour' (a book) to Gutnick T (2023) 'Cephalopod behaviour' in Current Biology. Listing those as FOUND_DIFFERS would say a work was found when a different work was.

changes.identified: in addition to the title thresholds, a record is the cited work only when its first-author surname agrees with the string, or its title token set equals the cited one and its year agrees. A record that passes the title thresholds and fails this is kept on the work as 'candidate' and the work is treated as a miss.
changes.compared_items: volume or pages that the record does not give are listed under not_compared ('record gives none'), not as a difference.
changes.miss_label: the book / non-biomedical markers are read in the work's text after its '(year)', not in the author names. (The first run read 'Wiley et al.' as the publisher Wiley; that was an implementation error against the declared rule.)

amendments.not_changed: states, scope, search steps, title thresholds, string_state, registry shape. A record by the same first author with a similar but different title still counts as identified and is listed with its differences; it may be a different work by that author, and the difference list is what shows it.

amendments.name: UNDERSPECIFIED + MATCH_SUSPECT; second index; abstract pass (stage 1b + stage 2)
amendments.after: the existence check at 1cd1cc8, whose results were seen; by the owner's order. Declared before any second-index search was sent and before any abstract was fetched. Reachability was probed first with one known paper: Europe PMC answered; api.openalex.org was refused by this environment's egress proxy (HTTP 403 on CONNECT).

existence_states_added.UNDERSPECIFIED: the work's text gives no quoted title and no venue, or the string names no work with an author and a year. Not searchable; it is not searched and it is not a miss. Distinct from NOT_FOUND_INDEXED, which now means a titled work was searched and no record identified. An untitled work whose description query returned exactly one record keeps the earlier rule (none occurred).
existence_states_added.MATCH_SUSPECT: a record was identified by first author, but the cited title's tokens (3+ letters, in order) are not a contiguous run inside the record's title and the year or the venue differs: plausibly a different work by the same author. The record and its differences are kept; the work is not counted as found. Written after the Dorigo & Gambardella (1997) row was seen, at the owner's direction.
existence_states_added.string_state_order: weakest first: UNDERSPECIFIED, NOT_FOUND_INDEXED, NOT_INDEXED, MATCH_SUSPECT, FOUND_DIFFERS, FOUND_AS_CITED
existence_states_added.lead: a work may carry 'lead': a hand-entered note from registry/existence_leads.json, marked as recall and unverified. Entered for Dorigo & Gambardella (1997): '1997 IEEE TEC 1:53-66 may exist as cited outside PubMed (recall, unverified)'.

second_index.scope: works in state NOT_FOUND_INDEXED, NOT_INDEXED or MATCH_SUSPECT after the re-sort. UNDERSPECIFIED works are not searched.
second_index.order: Europe PMC REST search (ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search, resultType lite); then OpenAlex for what is still not found. OpenAlex is unreachable here, so it is recorded as NOT_REACHED for each such work, never as a miss.
second_index.search: the same three steps as PubMed: AUTH + PUB_YEAR + TITLE words; AUTH + TITLE words; TITLE words. Same title words, at most 5 records.
second_index.identified: the same rule as PubMed after its amendment (title thresholds 0.8 / 0.5; first author agrees, or equal title with agreeing year), then the MATCH_SUSPECT test. No rule is changed after the run; an error found in the adapter is recorded as an error, not folded in silently.
second_index.control: one known paper (Sumbre 2001, PMID 11546877) is used to confirm the adapter reads the response shape. It is already FOUND_AS_CITED and is not in scope.
second_index.recorded: each searched work gains second_index {index, queries, state, matched_record, differs, not_compared, candidate}. When the second index identifies the work as FOUND_AS_CITED or FOUND_DIFFERS, the work's state becomes that state and matched_record names the index; the PubMed outcome is kept under 'pubmed'. Otherwise the work's state does not change.

abstract_pass.scope: works identified in PubMed and not suspect: 8 FOUND_AS_CITED and 4 FOUND_DIFFERS (12 works, 11 attribute fields). Works found only in the second index are not in this pass.
abstract_pass.fetch: NCBI efetch, db=pubmed, rettype=abstract. Abstract only; no full text. Abstract text is not committed; its sha256 is listed in provenance/as_received/abstracts_MANIFEST.json.
abstract_pass.reader: the abstracts are read by the model writing this entry; each judgment is entered by hand in registry/attribute_readings.json with a verbatim quote of at most 25 words. One reader, no second reading.

judgment.STATES: the abstract states the field's value or the claim in the field's definition -> status 'OBSERVED (basis: abstract)'
judgment.RELATED: the abstract is on the subject and does not state the value -> status 'PROPOSED', with a note
judgment.CONTRADICTS: the abstract contradicts the value or claim -> the value is kept, status 'PROPOSED', note 'contradicted by abstract'
judgment.NO_ABSTRACT: the record has no abstract -> no status change

abstract_pass.what_is_judged: the field's value together with its scope.definition in the entity file. A numeric value is 'stated' only when the abstract gives that number or one that rounds to it for the defined quantity.
abstract_pass.several_works: a field backed by more than one read work takes OBSERVED only when at least one abstract STATES it and none CONTRADICTS; a CONTRADICTS from any read abstract gives PROPOSED with the note. Works of the same string that were not read are named in the note.
abstract_pass.mechanism: entity files are not edited. registry/attribute_readings.json is an overlay read by scripts/provenance_chain.py: an attribute field with a reading gets that status, a status_note, and params.status_basis {read, source_id, pmids}. Status is in the step id, so build appends a new step that supersedes the old one; the old step stays.
abstract_pass.registry: a source string with at least one work read gets opened = 'abstract', fetched = the date, and opened_note = how many of its works were read. Strings are not edited.
abstract_pass.evidence_type_table: still NOT APPLIED. These statuses come from reading.

exports.reference: re-exported; no rule change. Status 'OBSERVED (basis: abstract)' reads OBSERVED.
exports.examples: attribute fields with a status are example targets with role observation (the earlier entry listed null attributes only). An OBSERVED example's status starts with 'OBSERVED'. Filters otherwise unchanged.
exports.holdout: the stratified rule is re-applied unchanged, not re-chosen
exports.blind: blind/ is left as built at 4221e16; it is a frozen package and is not rebuilt when the reference moves
